look_here_first: CEREAL RYE (INTRODUCED): find a fibrous-rooted cool-season cereal with one narrow unbranched, often awned terminal SPIKE, not a branched oat panicle. Follow the rachis: ONE sessile spikelet alternates at each node, usually containing TWO fertile florets (sometimes a reduced third). Under 10–20× verify two narrow one-veined awl-like glumes, and five-veined sharply keeled lemmas with rough/ciliate keels and long terminal awns. At the true leaf collar check a short MEMBRANOUS ligule and small auricles when present. Hordeum has THREE spikelets per node; wheat has broader multi-flowered spikelets; wildryes have paired spikelets. Not a Hays-native restoration grass.

best_field_traits: CEREAL RYE is a cultivated/escaped INTRODUCED cool-season cereal grass with long narrow terminal spikes and rows of overlapping spikelets bearing long awns; each spikelet usually has two fertile florets. Contrast with Hordeum pusillum: true barley makes triads of 3 spikelets at rachis nodes. Rye is not a Hays-native restoration grass.
RACHIS: ONE sessile, typically TWO-fertile-flowered spikelet at each alternating node of a two-ranked unbranched terminal spike; do not confuse florets with spikelets.
GLUMES: two narrow awl-like 1-veined bracts, FNA genus 8–20 mm (NZ cultivated treatment 7–12.5 mm), with scabrous/ciliate keel and short awnlet often 1–3 mm.
LEMMAS: firm five-veined, sharply keeled, usually ~14–18 mm in Australian treatment; conspicuously pectinate-ciliate keel and upper margins; long terminal lemma awn ~20–50 mm (other treatments vary).
TRUE COLLAR: short truncate/lacerate membranous ligule (~0.5–1.5 mm in NZ cultivated treatment); small auricles often present, sometimes obscure. Annual/biennial fibrous roots, no creeping rhizomes.

crew_field_check: Little barley (Hordeum pusillum) has triple spikelets at each rachis node and a much smaller tuft, whereas Secale cereale has a large continuous spike with individual 2-flowered spikelets alternating along the axis; distinguish from wheat Triticum aestivum by bract features, glumes and cereal head morphology.
Count ONE spikelet per rye rachis node versus THREE one-flowered spikelets at each barley node; inside rye spikelet count usually TWO fertile florets.
Distinguish short glume awnlets from much longer terminal LEMMA awns; inspect rough comb-ciliate lemma keel.
Inspect true inner collar ligule and small auricles; head shape/awn length alone cannot separate cultivated or escaped cereals.

diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.look_here_first: CEREAL RYE (INTRODUCED): find a fibrous-rooted cool-season cereal with one narrow unbranched, often awned terminal SPIKE, not a branched oat panicle. Follow the rachis: ONE sessile spikelet alternates at each node, usually containing TWO fertile florets (sometimes a reduced third). Under 10–20× verify two narrow one-veined awl-like glumes, and five-veined sharply keeled lemmas with rough/ciliate keels and long terminal awns. diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.growth_form: Cool-season fibrous-rooted annual or occasionally biennial cereal, commonly ~50–150 cm in NZ treatment; no rhizomes.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.spike_and_spikelets: Two-ranked unbranched spike, ~4–30 cm in NZ treatment; ONE sessile spikelet per rachis node, usually TWO fertile florets, sometimes reduced third; FNA genus spikelet 10–18 mm.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.glumes: Two narrow, 1-veined, rough-keeled awl-like glumes: 8–20 mm in FNA genus, 7–12.5 mm in NZ cultivated subsp. cereale; glume awnlets often ~1–3 mm. Source ranges differ.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.fertile_lemma: Five-veined firm, strongly keeled lemma, commonly 14–18 mm in Australian treatment (broader 10–20 mm NZ); comb-like cilia on keel and margins; terminal awn ~20–50 mm in Australian treatment, ~15–65 mm in NZ.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.ligule_and_collar: Short membranous, often truncate/lacerate ligule, ~0.5–1.5 mm NZ; small auricles often present (~0.5–1 mm in FNA genus), but sometimes obscure. Check actual junction.
local_lookalikes: Hordeum pusillum: THREE one-flowered spikelets per rachis node, versus ONE usually two-flowered rye spikelet.
Triticum aestivum: broader multi-flowered spikelets and broader glumes; examine attached node and lemma keel, not head color.
Elymus virginicus: paired multi-flowered spikelets at nodes with different glume bases; do not infer rye from slender awns.
Avena fatua: open branched panicle with hanging spikelets and bent dorsal lemma awns.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Cereal rye — ear first, spikelet next, collar last
steps: First follow the source-labelled rye flowering ear and long awns in the overview photograph. Do not infer the exact number of florets or awn origin from a distant ear.

Use the two physically stored Matt Lavin rye spikelet photographs to learn where narrow glumes enclose larger florets; their fine structures are source-labelled and still require pixel-level verification before individual arrows.

On the same mature plant, open the blade–sheath junction and photograph the auricles, ligule membrane, and sheath margins with a 1-mm scale. The current three photos do not provide a verified collar macro.
Compare mature rye and other cereal grasses using actual spikelet arrangement and glume/lemma anatomy, not long awns alone.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Three genuine archived JPEGs; two are source-labelled rye spikelet anatomy but not confirmed measured dissection. No true auricle or ligule close-up and no new microscopic arrows.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: An intact rye ear, narrow glumes and awned florets are useful together, with leaf auricles and ligule checked on the same specimen. Do not certify from an awned head alone.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — UNBRANCHED RYE SPIKE
field_id_short_tiles.short: One narrow two-ranked terminal spike, not a loose branched oat panicle.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Follow the central rachis on the attached head. Each successive node bears ONE sessile spikelet in alternating rows; each spikelet normally contains TWO fertile florets (a reduced third may occur). New photo panels 1–2 show source-labelled rye spikelet anatomy, but a same-stem attached rachis node is still missing. Cultivated rye is introduced, not a Hays-native restoration species.
field_id_short_tiles.status: SOURCE-IDENTIFIED PHOTO — ATTACHED NODE STILL NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · ROOTED ANNUAL AND ACTUAL COLLAR
field_id_short_tiles.short: Fibrous-rooted cool-season cereal; short 0.5–1.5 mm membranous ligule, sometimes small auricles.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Find the true blade/sheath seam on the same rooted plant. New Zealand's cultivated rye treatment gives a short 0.5–1.5 mm ligule and short auricles; VicFlora reports a 1–2 mm membrane. The auricles may be obscure. No existing gallery panel proves this small membrane with a 1-mm ruler or a connected rooted crown.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · COUNT SPIKELETS PER RACHIS NODE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Rye = ONE usually two-flowered spikelet per node; barley = THREE one-flowered spikelets.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Examine a complete intact node at 10–20× before separating spikelets. The one-versus-three SPIKELET comparison is more reliable than counting apparent awns in a crowded head. Wheat can also have one spikelet per node but generally has more florets and broader glumes. Panels 1–2 show detached source-labelled spikelets, not a proven attached node with a ruler.
field_id_short_tiles.status: DETACHED SPIKELET PHOTOS — NODE MICRO MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · GLUMES, LEMMAS AND DIFFERENT AWNS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Two narrow one-veined glumes ~7–12.5 mm in NZ; firm five-veined lemmas ~10–20 mm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Dissect a mature spikelet and isolate the two stiff rough-keeled glumes (NZ 7–12.5 mm; broader Flora of North America genus 8–20 mm), each with a short glume awnlet. The lemma has a comb-ciliate keel and a much longer terminal awn (NZ 15–65 mm). Do not call the glume awnlet a fertile lemma awn. Existing panels do not resolve all veins or both awn origins at a calibrated scale.
field_id_short_tiles.status: SOURCE-BASED MEASUREMENTS — DISSECTION WITH SCALE MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Little barley = triple spikelets; wild oat = branched panicle; wheat/wildrye need node dissection.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Hordeum pusillum has THREE one-flowered spikelets at a rachis node. Avena fatua has a loose branched panicle and dorsal bent/twisted lemma awns. Triticum aestivum has broader multi-flowered spikelets; Elymus virginicus bears paired spikelets at nodes. Use same-stage attached rachis nodes and glume shapes, not brown head color or awn length alone.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE AND EXACT HANDOFF
field_id_short_tiles.short: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS — three archived source photos preserved; no new photo or arrow evidence.
field_id_short_tiles.details: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: same verified rooted rye with complete mature spike and ruler; opened collar showing 0.5–1.5 mm ligule and auricles with 1-mm scale; one attached node with ONE two-flowered spikelet at 10–20×; isolated one-veined glumes, five-veined comb-ciliate lemma and distinct short glume awnlet versus long terminal lemma awn; matched barley/wheat/wildrye nodes. NEEDS_SITE_QA: confirm all three physically archived JPEGs, Gavin Schaefer CC BY-NC rights, Matt Lavin CC BY-SA 2.0 attribution, two preexisting gross arrows and ordinary public learner tile/mobile rendering. Do not mark FINISHED without pixel-resolved anatomy.
